title: The Unwritten Typewriter
premise: In 1934, on a storm-battered island off the northern coast, widowed lighthouse keeper Juniper Ashgrove lives quietly, tending the light and avoiding questions. When census taker Aldous Wren arrives and notices that the 'widow' Ashgrove is a man living under his dead wife's identity, he becomes an unwilling accomplice: hidden inside the lighthouse is a typewriter whose ribbon holds evidence of coastal smuggling run by the very officials who control the checkpoints to the mainland. To survive, Juniper must smuggle the ribbon past three inspections before the annual supply boat — and the inspector who murdered his wife's brother — departs with it destroyed. In the end, Juniper sacrifices the lighthouse itself, burning it as a signal fire that exposes the smugglers, and boards the boat under his own name for the first time in nine years.
about_author: Emrys Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime records from remote northern stations. Fascinated by the small bureaucratic paper trails that decide ordinary lives, they write historical fiction about people erased by their own documents.

chapters.title: The Light That Answers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A routine night keeping the lamp during early autumn gales establishes his isolation, his rituals, and the careful way he signs logs as 'J. Ashgrove, widow.' Emotional beat: quiet grief and practiced invisibility.

chapters.title: A Man Who Counts Heads
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Census taker Aldous Wren arrives on the supply boat, cheerful and observant. He asks for the keeper's full name and date of marriage; Juniper's answers falter. Beat: first crack in the armor.

chapters.title: What the Widow Kept
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, flashback woven in. We learn how Maren Ashgrove died and why Juniper took her name: her brother Tomas was a customs clerk who vanished after finding discrepancies in cargo manifests. Beat: guilt sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: The Ribbon in the Case
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Curious rather than hostile, Wren explores the boathouse and finds an old typewriter, its ribbon still inked with fragments of manifest numbers matching records he audited years ago. Beat: fascination turning to dread.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Confrontation in the kitchen: Wren reveals what the ribbon implies — that Inspector Corvane, now overseeing all mainland checkpoints, signed off the falsified manifests the night Tomas disappeared. Beat: two lonely men bound by a secret.

chapters.title: The Supply Boat Schedule
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The last boat before winter leaves in eleven days; Corvane himself will inspect it. Wren proposes smuggling the ribbon out as evidence. Juniper refuses — until a patrol launch circles the island too long. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Maren's Hands
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Searching Maren's sewing box for hiding places, he finds her letters proving she knew Tomas's suspicions. He realizes she died protecting him, not fleeing him. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Harbor Master
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. First attempt: the ribbon sewn into a coil of lamp wick. The harbor master, drunk and bored, nearly passes them — then asks Wren why a census taker travels with a keeper's trunk. Beat: escape by a lie that costs Wren his cover story.

chapters.title: The Man Who Drowned Twice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the mainland road, Wren confesses his own secret: he falsified a drowning verdict years ago under Corvane's orders, and this mission is his penance. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made personal.

chapters.title: Corvane's Winter List
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (first antagonist view). Cold, meticulous, he reviews names flagged at checkpoint one — including 'the Ashgrove widow' — and orders the lighthouse logbook seized. Beat: the net tightening.

chapters.title: Back Across the Water
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Forced to return for the logbook before Corvane's men reach it, Juniper rows through a rising storm, hallucinating Maren at the tiller. Beat: the sea as memory and judge.

chapters.title: The Empty Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He reaches the lighthouse to find the logbook gone but the typewriter disturbed — someone else has read the ribbon. A note in Tomas's handwriting, dated three days ago. Beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Tomas Ashgrove, alive and hiding as a fisherman, reveals he has been shadowing Corvane for years but needed proof only the ribbon provides. His survival reopens every wound between him and Juniper. Beat: reunion as reckoning.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Toll Bridge
chapters.summary: Three POVs converge. With the ribbon hidden in Wren's census ledger itself, they cross the toll bridge; Corvane's clerk inspects papers while Tomas creates a diversion that goes wrong. Beat: sacrifice — Tomas is taken.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren wants to turn back for Tomas; Juniper argues the evidence matters more than any one life — echoing the choice that haunts them both. They quarrel bitterly. Beat: the alliance fractures.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Records House
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane burns the archived manifests, erasing the paper trail, confident the ribbon alone proves nothing without context. Beat: villain at the height of power, and the reader sees the clock run down.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Quay
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Final inspection at the winter boat's quay. Corvane searches Juniper personally, finds nothing — because the ribbon is threaded through the boat's own signal flag halyard. Beat: triumph undercut by Corvane's parting threat.

chapters.title: Nine Years Under Her Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, quiet interlude aboard the boat. He writes a confession letter to Maren's memory, deciding that if the evidence lands, he will surrender his false name willingly. Beat: acceptance before the storm.

chapters.title: The Signal Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Corvane intercepts the boat offshore; the ribbon's location is betrayed by a shaken crewman. Juniper ignites the abandoned lighthouse — visible for forty miles — the prearranged signal that sends journalists and naval inspectors waiting on the mainland straight to the quay. Beat: everything burned to save the truth.

chapters.title: Arrests at Dawn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Corvane is taken on the quay; Tomas, released when the clerk panics, identifies the manifest pages from memory. Wren gives testimony about his old false verdict, accepting his own charges. Beat: justice with a bill attached.

chapters.title: Juniper Ashgrove, Keeper
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Standing before the charred tower, he signs his statement with both names — the one he was born with and the one he kept. He chooses to rebuild the light. Beat: identity reclaimed, not discarded.

chapters.title: The Unwritten Page
chapters.summary: Epilogue, spring. Juniper, Tomas, and Wren load a new typewriter onto the rebuilt station; its fresh ribbon is blank. Juniper begins writing the true account of the great storms. Final beat: survival's price paid, and the page finally his own.
